Note Note: A client in receipt of CPP and OAS benefits may receive more than one type of tax slip for the same calendar year. For example, if a client was a resident of Canada for part of the year and then became a non-resident for the rest of that same year, they will receive a T4A and an NR4 for that taxation year for both CPP and OAS. For an OAS pension and income-tested benefits, an NR4 tax slip must be issued separately for each benefit for periods when the client was a non-resident.
Note Note: For OAS, do not edit the Preferred method of tax slips correspondence field in Cúram. Clients must use the Client Portal via MSCA if they wish to modify their tax slip preference.

Note Note: If the priority payment was issued in the previous calendar year but was not recorded in Cúram until the following year (e.g. a payment is issued in 2025 but was recorded in Cúram in 2026), then the tax slip must be amended and issued in Cúram.

Note Note: As of the end of December 2025, the OAS/IA Adjustment screen in ITRDS is no longer available to be viewed or modified. To make any modifications to the 2025 year- to-date amounts, the final tax slip must be amended in Cúram.

Note Note: A GIS overpayment recovered from an OAS benefit will not reduce the amount of the OAS benefit paid to the client. As the GIS is a non-taxable benefit, it cannot be used to decrease taxable income.

Callout Example After you put the applicant into pay for the PRDB , the applicant appeals the CPPD benefits application decision because they disagree with the Date of Onset (DOO). At the reconsideration level, the DOO is determined to be before the RTR pension start date. The Department approves a change of benefit from the PRDB to the DSB because: the applicant is in pay for an RTR pension for less than 15 months at the date of application for the DSB ; the applicant is under the age of 65; the applicant has a severe and prolonged disability, as defined in the Canada Pension Plan legislation; and the DOO is before the start date of the RTR pension.

Note Note: If the applicant is in pay for an RTR pension and they submit a CPPD benefits application, the Department must use the CPPD benefits application to determine if the client is eligible for a DSB or PRDB .

Add an important note in ITRDS indicating that the decision on the CPPD benefits application is reversed and granted at the reconsideration level and that the PRDB and DCCPR benefit (if applicable) are cancelled. Callout Example A student submits a completed ISP-1402 form and it is approved. The school year starts September 2024 and ends April 2025. To support their claim they submit an ISP-1403 form to confirm they cannot resume full-time attendance at school during that academic year. You must not suspend the child's benefit in this situation as the child is deemed to be in full-time attendance until the end of the school vacation period (i.e. until September 2025).

Callout Example A student submits an ISP-1402 form and it is approved. The school year starts in September 2024 and ends in June 2025. The vacation period starts in July 2025 and ends in September 2025. In December 2024, the student stops attending school due to an illness. To support their claim, they submit an ISP-1403 form that covers the 2024-2025 academic year and vacation period. Their child's benefit payments will continue for the remainder of the 2024-2025 academic year, including the summer vacation period. The student does not resume school attendance during the 2025-2026 or 2026-2027 academic years but is able to return to school or university on a full-time basis in the 2027-2028 school year. Due to this, the student cannot be considered to have been in full-time attendance for the 2025-2026 school year, even though they were deemed as attending full-time during their illness period from December 2024 to September 2025. To be entitled, the student must have submitted an ISP-1403 form and resumed attendance immediately after the period of illness. If the student is absent for the entire year, they will only be entitled to benefits if they resume attendance in the following academic year and submit a second ISP-1403 form to support the entire period of the absence (including the vacation period).

Callout Example 1 The current system accounting month is October 2024. The Correctional Service of Canada data transfer indicates that the client was incarcerated on October 2, 2024. You must place the account on hold until the November 2025 accounting month as the client is entitled to receive their pension payment for November 2024. In the November 2024 accounting month, the account must be suspended.

Callout Example 2 The Correctional Service of Canada monthly data transfer lists the client’s date of incarceration as January 15, 2024. Based on this information, the client’s OAS benefits must be suspended effective February 2024, the month following the month of their date of incarceration.

Callout Example 1 In August 2024, a letter is received from a client notifying the Department that they were released from a federal penitentiary on July 15, 2024. The release date indicated on the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer is also July 15, 2024. The information is a match. A review of the client’s file confirms that they were in pay for the OAS pension and the GIS before they were incarcerated, and that they continue to meet all the eligibility requirements for the benefits. The CRA 2023 income feed has been received. The client’s OAS pension and GIS are reinstated effective July 2024, the month of their release from incarceration.

Callout Example 2 In November 2024, the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer indicates that the client was released from incarceration in October 2024. A review of the Department's systems confirms that the client was in receipt of the OAS pension and the GIS before their incarceration, but they have not yet advised the Department of their release. The client has a spouse who has been receiving the ALW benefit based on their individual income as the rate is to their advantage while the pensioner was incarcerated. The ALW benefit is reverted to being calculated on the couple’s combined income effective October 2024. Since the account is being adjusted in November 2024, an overpayment for the month of October 2024 is established. The pensioner’s account remains suspended and is placed on hold for 30 days awaiting written notification of their release. On November 30, 2024, the written notification of release is received from the client and the release date provided is confirmed as a match with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client's OAS pension and GIS account is reviewed and they continue to be eligible to receive the OAS pension and the GIS . The benefits are reinstated effective October 2024, the month of their release from incarceration.

Callout Example 1 The client was incarcerated on February 15, 2018, and was released from incarceration on April 11, 2023. The incarceration dates were confirmed with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client turned 65 on March 6, 2021. In April 2023, upon their release from incarceration, they applied for their OAS pension and indicated that they have lived in Canada since birth. In normal circumstances, the client would be entitled to 24 months of actuarial adjustment for the period of April 2021 (the earliest date of eligibility) and their effective date of April 2023 (the month of their release). However, since this client has been incarcerated since 2018 (i.e. before their 65th birthday), they are not entitled to any deferral for the period of April 2021 to April 2023.

Callout Example 2 The client was incarcerated on November 12, 2020, and was released from incarceration on July 5, 2024. The incarceration dates were confirmed with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client turned 65 on November 16, 2022. On August 12, 2024, after being released from incarceration, the client applied for their OAS pension and the GIS . The client is not entitled to the GIS as their income is in excess. They have provided the following residence history: Birth to May 31, 1993: Italy June 1, 1993 to present: Canada In normal circumstances, the client would receive a choice between: 31/40ths effective July 2024; or 29/40ths with 19 months of actuarial adjustment effective July 2024. Since this client was incarcerated before their 65th birthday, the residence can accumulate up until the month the pension is approved. However, the client is not entitled to accrue an actuarial adjustment for the months they were incarcerated. Therefore, in this situation, no pension choices would be offered to the client. Their pension would be approved effective July 2024 at a rate of 31/40ths.

Reminder: International Social Security Agreements Reminder: International Social Security Agreements Most of Canada's International Social Security Agreements (ISSA) include a provision that provides, under specified conditions, the date of receipt of an application for a benefit payable by one country can be deemed as the date of receipt of an application for the corresponding benefit of the other country. Therefore, the date of receipt of a foreign benefit application may be deemed as the date of the corresponding CPP or OAS benefit application, if certain conditions are met. In these cases, the deemed date of application should be considered when determining if the CPP or OAS benefit application should be treated as a post-mortem application. For instance, a post-mortem CPP RTR pension application is received on March 15, 2023, on behalf of a contributor who died on November 9, 2021. The Social Security Agreement's (SSA) partner country's social security administration confirms the date of application for the corresponding benefit is April 23, 2020. Assuming the conditions under the SSA have been met, for administrative purposes, including those related to system input, the CPP RTR pension date of application is deemed as April 23, 2020.

Callout Example 1 John is a disabled contributor who turned 65 years old in January 2025. At the time, John had decision-making responsibility and parenting time of Catherine, their niece who was under the age of 18. As a result, John continued to receive the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) on behalf of Catherine. In March 2025, John notifies the Department in writing that they no longer have decision-making responsibility and parenting time of Catherine. As John is over 65 years old and the child-contributor relationship between John and Catherine ended, there is no longer entitlement to the DCCB . In June 2025, John sends in a new Application for Benefits for Under Age 18 Children of Disabled Contributor (ISP-1152) form as Catherine returned to their care in May 2025. The Department notifies John in writing that there is no entitlement to the DCCB on behalf of Catherine as the child-contributor relationship ended after John's 65th birthday. To be eligible, the child-contributor relationship needed to be continuous after turning 65 years of age.

Callout Example 2 In April 2025 the Department was notified that Sarah, John's child who is over the age of 18 (+18 child), stopped attending school in March 2025. This resulted in the DCCB being terminated. DCCB was originally extended because Sarah was attending school the month John reached age 65 in January 2025. In September 2025, Sarah returned to school and submitted a new Application for a Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit and Declaration for a student over 18 years of age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402-A) form. The Department notified Sarah that since there was a break in school attendance, there is no eligibility for the DCCB . A child is no longer considered a dependant once their school attendance ends. At the time Sarah submitted the declaration of attendance, the CPPD benefit was no longer in pay and Sarah was not eligible.

Callout Example 3 Mark, a disabled contributor in receipt of the PRDB , turned 65 years old in February 2025. At the time, Liam, Mark's +18 child was attending school part-time. Due to this, Liam's DCCB eligibility was extended until their current school attendance ends in April 2025. The school period was entered in ITRDS as January 2025 to September 2025. The Department sent Liam a new ISP-1402-A form in August 2025. However, Liam did not return the form until January 2026. The information on the form regarding Liam's school attendance shows that Liam attended school full-time from September to December 2025. It also shows that Liam is currently enrolled full-time for the January 2026 to April 2026 semester. As there is no break in school attendance, Liam's DCCB can be reinstated and put into pay effective October 2025 until September 2026.

Callout Example 4 Mark, a disabled contributor in receipt of a PRDB , reached age 65 in February 2025. The Department received an ISP-1152 form in March 2025 on behalf of Mark's grandson Keith. Keith only came into Mark's care after Mark turned 65 years of age. Eligibility requirements for DCCB require the disabled contributor to be under the age of 65 at the time the child-contributor relationship begins. As this requirement was not met, the Department denied the application and informed Mark in writing of the eligibility requirements.

Callout Example 5 The Department received an ISP-1402-A form in January 2025 from Simone. Simone's mother was receiving a PRDB until she turned 65 years old in December 2024. Since Simone's mother turned 65 years old before January 1, 2025, the Department cannot extend Simone's eligibility for DCCB . The discretion to consider an individual who is married or in a common-law partnership to be paid at the single rate is intended for exceptional circumstances where applicants or pensioners cannot obtain their spouse or common-law partner's initial signature or their income information in order to calculate their GIS. Because of the discretionary nature of the decision, it is not possible to provide an exhaustive list all of the circumstances that may suffice to pay the GIS at the single rate. Such circumstances where it would be unreasonable to require the spouse or common-law partner's signature or income may include the applicant or pensioner's fear for their safety (e.g. situations of mental or physical abuse), situations where the spouse or common-law partner is a hostage, lost or missing, or other exceptional circumstances.

Note Reminder: In cases where a decision is made to pay the GIS at the single rate, the account must be reviewed annually to see if the circumstances have changed and attempts must be made to obtain the spouse or common-law partner's signature and income.

Callout Example 1 A CPPD benefits application with a child under the age of 18 (-18 child) listed on the application is submitted. The CPPD application is approved, and the incapacity provision is applied, deeming the application to have been received 3 years earlier. Does the earlier deemed Date of Application also apply to the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit (DCCB)? Yes , the incapacity provision applies to a -18 child listed on a CPPD benefits application.

Callout Example 2 A CPPD benefits application with a child over the age of 18 (+18 child) listed on the application is submitted. The CPPD application is approved, and the incapacity provision is applied, deeming the application to have been received 3 years earlier. The +18 child was determined to be over the age of 18 at the deemed earlier date of application. Does the earlier deemed DOA also apply to the DCCB? Yes , the incapacity provision can apply to a +18 child listed on a CPPD benefits application. The disabled contributor must provide their written consent to contact the child. The +18 child must submit their application and confirmation of school attendance within the prescribed Bring Forward (BF) timeframes.

Callout Example 3 New A CPPD benefits application with a +18 child listed on the application is submitted. The CPPD application is approved and the incapacity provision is applied to the disabled contributor, deeming the application to have been received 3 years earlier. At the deemed earlier DOA, the now +18 child was then under the age of 18. Is the applicant eligible for -18 DCCB at the deemed earlier DOA, if all other criteria are met? Yes , if the child was under age 18 at the earlier deemed DOA and is listed on the CPPD benefits application, they are eligible for-18 DCCB. To continue to be paid +18 DCCB, they would have to submit their application and confirmation of school attendance within the prescribed BF timeframes.

Callout Example 4 An applicant turned 65 years of age in January 2016. The applicant became totally incapacitated in May 2014 because of a car accident. An application for an OAS pension is completed on their behalf in May 2017 and includes a Declaration of Incapacity - Physician's Report (ISP-1800) form. The file is forwarded to a Medical Adjudicator (MA) for review. The MA determines that the applicant was incapacitated in May 2014 and returns the file to the SCBO for processing. Because the date of incapacity is before the applicant's 65th birthday, the deemed date of receipt is January 2016. As a result, you must use this date, and not May 2017, to calculate the entitlement. In addition, if all legislative requirements are met, the effective date can be as early as February 2016, i.e. the month following the applicant's 65th birthday.

Callout Example 5 An applicant turned 65 years of age in April 2014. In October 2015, they suffered a severe stroke that left them totally incapacitated as of that month. An application for an RTR pension is filed on their behalf in March 2016 and includes an ISP-1800 form. The file is forwarded to a MA for review. The MA determines that the applicant was incapacitated in October 2015 and returns the file to the SCBO for processing. As a result, you must use October 2015, and not March 2016, to calculate the entitlement. In addition, if all legislative requirements are met, the effective date for benefits can be as early as November 2014. This effective date is based on 11 months retroactively from the deemed date of receipt of October 2015. For more information, Effective Date—Retirement Pension (Policy)

Callout Example 6: The application must be submitted within one month after regaining capacity if the period of incapacity was less than 30 days An applicant was involved in a motor vehicle accident on June 15, 2018. After 28 days, the applicant had recovered from their coma but remained disabled. They applied for CPPD benefits in December 2019 and requested the benefit to be retroactive to June 2018 based on their incapacity. Table 4. The facts Event Date Start date of incapacity June 15, 2018 End date of incapacity July 13, 2018 Duration of the incapacity 28 days Date of Application (DOA) December 2019 Earliest Possible Date of Onset (EPDOO) September 2018 Since the applicant was incapacitated for less than one month, an application for CPPD benefits must be received within one month of regaining capacity. In this scenario, it would be August 13, 2018. The application was received in December 2019, which was not within the specified timeframe of on or before August 13, 2018. The Incapacity provision cannot be used to provide the applicant with a new earlier deemed DOA.

Callout Example 7: The application must be submitted within the number of days equal to the number of days the person was incapacitated if the period was less than one year On May 1, 2013, an applicant was involved in an industrial accident and sustained a severe head injury. The applicant remained hospitalized and unresponsive until April 25, 2014. The incapacity lasted less than 12 months. Table 5. The facts Event Date Start date of incapacity May 1, 2013 End date of incapacity April 25, 2014 Duration of incapacity 359 days (under 365 days) CPPD benefits DOA January 2017 EPDOO October 1, 2015 To be considered for a benefit under the Incapacity provision, an application for a benefit must have been submitted within 359 days of April 25, 2014, which is April 19, 2015. Since the applicant submitted a CPPD benefits application in January 2017, the Incapacity provision cannot be considered because the DOA is outside of the timeframe to apply the provision, i.e. more than 359 days after the incapacity ended.

Callout Example 8: The application must be submitted within 12 months if the period of incapacity was greater than 12 months Scenario 1 On February 1, 2015, an applicant had an acute event and remained hospitalized and in a coma until September 1, 2016. The incapacity lasted more than 12 months. Table 6. The facts Event Date Start date of incapacity February 1, 2015 End date of incapacity September 1, 2016 Duration of incapacity Over 365 days CPPD benefits DOA January 1, 2019 To be considered for a benefit under the incapacity provision, an application for a benefit must have been submitted within 12 months of September 1, 2016, which is September 1, 2017. Since the applicant submitted a CPPD benefits application in January 2019, they are only entitled to receive maximum retroactivity from their actual DOA, which is January 1, 2019. However, the incapacity provision cannot be considered because the DOA is outside of the timeframe to apply the provision, i.e. more than 12 months after the incapacity ended. Scenario 2 An applicant became incapacitated because of a severe head injury in November 2015, 4 months after their 65th birthday in July 2015. After extensive treatment, the applicant recovered to the point of having regained capacity by December 2017. The applicant submits an application for an OAS pension in March 2018 with a note explaining their prior incapacity. A Declaration of Incapacity - Physician's Report (ISP-1800) form is sent to the applicant for completion. When it is returned to the Department, the completed file is sent to a Medical Adjudicator (MA) for review. The MA determines that the applicant was incapacitated from November 2015 to December 2017 and returns the file to the SCBO for processing. Table 7. The facts Event Date Start date of incapacity November 1, 2015 End date of incapacity December 1, 2017 Duration of incapacity Over 365 days Because the Department received the application within the required timeframe for consideration under the Incapacity provision, the deemed date of receipt is November 2015. You must use November 2015, and not March 2018, to calculate the entitlement. In addition, if all legislative requirements are met, the effective date can be as early as August 2015, which is the month following the applicant's 65th birthday.

Callout Example The client retired in April 2020. The client received the retirement pension from July to December 2020 (6 months) at $300.00 per month. Prorated amount: ($300.00 × 6) ∕ 8 × 12 = $2,700.00

Callout Example The client retired in April 2022. The client received the private pension effective May 2022 at $50.00 twice per month for 8 months. Prorated amount: {($50.00 x 2) × 8} ∕ 8 × 12 = $1,200.00

Callout Example The client retired in April 2021. The client received the private pension starting on May 19, 2021 at $50.00 bi-weekly for 34 weeks. Determine the calculated monthly amount of the private pension: ($50.00 × 26) ∕ 12 = $108.33 Prorate the private pension income using the calculated monthly amount in the formula: ($108.33 × 8) ∕ 8 × 12 = $1,299.96

Callout Example 1 The client retired in April 2021. The client began withdrawing weekly Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) payments on May 18, 2021 at $100.00 per week for a total of 34 weeks in 2021. Prorate the RRIF payments using the formula: ($100.00 × 34) ∕ 8 × 12 = $5,100.00 Calculate the maximum possible yearly amount : $100.00 × 52 = $5,200.00 Compare the results of Step 1 and Step 2 to determine the lesser amount: In this case, you must use the lesser amount of $5,100.00 from Step 1.

Callout Example 2 The client retired on October 4, 2020. The client received their first EI benefits payment of $100.00 on November 5, 2020 for the period of October 25 to 31. The client received their final payment on February 10, 2021 for the week of January 31 to February 6, 2021. Determine the number of full weeks from the effective date (November 1) to the end of the calendar year (December 31): 9 weeks Note: The calculation is based on full weeks only. If a partial week remains after counting all full weeks, consider it as one full week. Prorate the EI benefits using the formula: ($100.00 × 9) ∕ 2 × 12 = $5,400.00 Calculate the maximum possible yearly amount: $100.00 × 52 = $5,200.00 Compare the results of Step 1 and Step 2 to determine the lesser amount: In this case, you must use the lesser amount of $5,200.00 from Step 2. Note: EI benefits are paid bi-weekly, but a weekly rate is used by EI to determine how much the client will receive on their payment. Therefore, the calculation to prorate a weekly benefit is used for a current year option.

Callout Example 1—Quarterly pension reduction is the event The client receives quarterly pension payments of $1200.00 every February, May, August and November. In August 2021, the quarterly payments were reduced to $950.00. Determine the calculated monthly amount using the reduced rate: $950.00 ∕ 3 = $316.67 Prorate the reduced pension income using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. Since the client receives this pension quarterly, the effective date of the option is the beginning of the quarter in which the pension was reduced (July 2021): ($316.67 × 6) / 6 × 12 ∕ $3,800.04

Callout Example 2—Quarterly pension is not the event The client receives quarterly pension payments of $450.00 every January, April, July and September. In May 2021, the client retired from employment. Determine the calculated monthly amount: $450.00 ∕ 3 = $150.00 Prorate the pension using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. Callout Example 1—Semi-annual pension reduction is the event The client receives semi-annual pension payments of $3,200.00 every May and November. In May 2022, the semi-annual payments were reduced to $2,350.00. Determine the calculated monthly amount using the reduced rate: $2,350.00 ∕ 6 = $391.67 Prorate the reduced pension income using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. Since the client receives this pension semi-annually, the effective date of the option is the beginning of the semi-annual period in which the pension was reduced (January 2022): ($391.67 × 12) ∕ 12 × 12 = $4,700.04

Callout Example 2—Semi-annual pension is not the event The client receives semi-annual pension payments of $1,800.00 every April and September. In October 2021, the client retired from employment. Determine the calculated monthly amount: $1,800 ∕ 6 = $300.00 Prorate the pension using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. The effective date of the option is November 2021: ($300.00 × 2) ∕ 2 × 12 = $3,600.00

Callout Example 1—Annual pension reduction is the event The client receives annual pension payments of $5,400.00 every May. In 2022, the annual payment is reduced to $4,400.00. Determine the calculated monthly amount using the reduced rate: $4,400.00 ∕ 12 = $366.67 Prorate the reduced pension income using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. Since the client receives this pension annually, the effective date of the option is January 2022: ($366.67 × 12) ∕ 12 × 12 = $4,400.04

Callout Example 2—Annual pension is not the event The client receives annual Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) payments of $2,350.00 every September. The client also receives a CPP pension of $875.00 per month and a monthly private pension of $500.00. In August 2021, the client received their final monthly private pension payment of $500.00. Determine the calculated monthly RRIF amount: $2,350.00 ∕ 12 = $195.83 Prorate the CPP pension and RRIF payments using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. The effective date of the option is September 2021: CPP pension - ($875.00 × 4) ∕ 4 × 12 = $10,500.00 RRIF payments - ($195.83 × 4) ∕ 4 × 12 = $2,349.96 Total estimated income = $12,849.96

Callout Example 1—Irregular pension reduction is the event The client receives irregular RRIF payments. In 2020, they received the following payments: $1,200.00 in February $800.00 in June $2,800.00 in October Total for 2020 = $4,800.00 In 2021, the client received the following payments: $700.00 in January $2,200.00 in August $1,100.00 in December Total for 2021 = $4,000.00 In 2021, the total of the irregular payments was reduced. Determine the calculated monthly amount using the total reduced rate: $4,000.00 ∕ 12 = $333.33 Prorate the reduced pension income using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. Since the client received this pension annually, the effective date of the option is January 2021: ($333.33 × 12) ∕ 12 × 12 = $3,999.96

Callout Example 2—Irregular pension is not the event The client receives irregular RRIF payments. In 2021, they received the following payments: $3,200.00 in March $800.00 in June $1,800.00 in December Total for 2021 = $5,800.00 In September 2021, the client retired. Determine the calculated monthly amount using the total of the payments: $5,800.00 ∕ 12 = $483.33 Prorate the pension using the calculated monthly amount in the formula. The effective date of the option is October 2021: ($483.33 × 3) ∕ 3 × 12 = $5,799.96

Callout Example The client received Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) payments from January to May 2021 at $300.00 per month. Then in June, the client increased their monthly RRIF payment to $500.00. In February 2021, the client retired. The effective month of the option is March 2021. Callout Example : The client is in receipt of a combined RTR pension and SVR pension. There is one pending payable of $800.00 (Payable A ) and two existing receivables with a balance of $2,000.00 (Receivable C ) and $1,000.00 (Receivable D ) respectively. Each month, 25% is deducted from the RTR pension and the SVR pension. After re-adjudicating the account, a supplementary payable of $300.00 (Payable B ) is owed to the client. The user applies the override receivable recovery amount of $150.00 between $800.00 (Payable A ) and $2,000.00 (Receivable C ). Payable A is $800.00 Payable B is $300.00 Receivable C is $2,000.00 with a recurring recovery rate of 25% Receivable D is $1,000.00 with a recurring recovery rate of 25% Payable A ($800.00) plus Payable B ($300.00) is a combined gross payable of $1,100.00. Therefore: Payable A ($800.00) will apply the $150.00 one-time recovery to Receivable C ($2,000.00) = $150.00 Payable A ($800.00) × 25% recovery rate for Receivable D ($1,000.00) = $200.00 Payable B ($300.00) × 25% recovery rate for Receivable C ($2,000.00) = $75.00 Payable B ($300.00) × 25% Receivable D recovery rate = $75.00 $150.00 + $75.00 = $225.00 is the combined deduction for Receivable C $75.00 + $200.00 = $275.00 is the combined deduction for Receivable D Gross payable $1,100.00 − $225.00 − $275.00 = Net payment of $600.00 (weekly payment)

Callout Example : The client is in receipt of a combined RTR pension and SVR pension. There is one existing payable of $800.00 along with two existing receivables with a balance of $2,000.00 and $1,000.00 respectively. Each month, 25% is deducted from the monthly RTR pension and SVR pension. After re-adjudicating the account, a supplementary payable of $300.00 is owed to the client. The supplementary payables of $800.00 and $300.00 will be issued as a weekly supplementary payable. The user applies the override receivable recovery amount of $150.00 between the $800.00 payable and the $2,000.00 receivable. $300.00 × 25% recovery rate = $75.00 $800.00 + $300.00 = $1,100.00 (gross payable) – $150.00 (one-time recovery) – $75.00 (recurring recovery) = Net Payment of $875.00 (weekly payment) Enquiries If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool (BERT) and select Canada Pension Plan & Old Age Security (access is required). Callout The CPP now consists of the following components: A base or original component (since January 1, 1966) that is calculated on earnings between the year's minimum and maximum amounts of pensionable earnings. The base contribution rate is 9.9% (4.95% from the employer and 4.95% from the employee). Self-employed individuals pay both the employer and employee amounts; and Additional or enhanced components which provide a top-up to the base and are broken down into first (effective January 1, 2019) and second (effective January 1, 2024). The first additional component is calculated on the same range of earnings as the base and has a total contribution rate of 2% (1% from the employer and 1% from the employee). Self-employed individuals pay both the employer and employee amounts. This additional rate was introduced gradually between 2019 and 2023 and will continue throughout a client's contributory period. The second additional component introduces a new range of earnings above the Year's Maximum Pensionable Earnings (YMPE). The contribution rate for this range of earnings will be 8% (4% employer and 4% employee) and will only be applied on earnings between the YMPE and the new earning limit or the ceiling (14% above YMPE), which is referred to as the Years Additional Maximum Pensionable Earnings (YAMPE). This increased earnings limit or the ceiling will be phased-in over 2 years between 2024 (YMPE plus 7%) and 2025 (YMPE plus 14%).

Note Note: Contributions and refund amounts may be calculated and adjusted by ESDC to ensure that contributors who did not file their tax returns can receive the enhanced component of CPP benefits in instances where the eligible contributor overcontributed and the T1 refund adjustments has not yet been received from CRA .

There is no requirement on the part of ESDC to report any discrepancies.

Callout Example When verifying a client’s CPP payments in CPMS for 2020, the following payments are displayed: January to June: $450.00 per month; July $1.550.00; and August to December: $550.00 per month. The total amount issued for CPP in 2020 is $7,000.00. This is the amount showing on their T4A(P) for 2020. The client was issued a retroactive payment of $1,000.00 for the period of September 2019 to July 2020. $400.00 of this lump sum payment is for 2019, the previous calendar year. Since the amount that extends to the previous calendar year is over $300.00, the notional tax provision can be applied. To calculate the client’s CPP amount applying the notional tax provision, perform the following calculation: Access CPMS or the IA system and determine the gross CPP rate for December 2020. Multiply the gross CPP rate for December by 12. ($550.00 x 12 = $6,600.00). Adjust the CPP amount in the system from $7000.00 to $6,600.00. The client’s 2020 CPP amount with the notional tax provision applied is $6,600.00. Performing this calculation removes the portion of the retroactive payment that relates to the previous year and ensures the client’s entitlement is based only on the income relating to the base calendar year.

This includes: Start Work: This task action moves a user's task from the Stopped Work / Work Not Started list to the Started Work list. Stop Work: This task action moves a user's task from the Started Work list to the Stopped Work / Work Not Started list. Add Comment : This task action allows a user to add comments to a task. Edit Task: This task action allows a user to update the category, type, skill type, and priority level of a task. Edit Due / Receipt Date: This task action allows a user to update the due date and receipt date of a task. Bring Forward: This task action allows a user to set the task to On Hold status until the bring forward date. This task will be allocated to the assigned work queue until the Bring Forward Date and will not show in the user's My Tasks list . Once the Bring Forward Date arrives, the system will set the task status back to Open . Make Available: This task action makes the task available to the previous assigned. The user will no longer see the task in their My Open Tasks list. Forward: This task action allows a user to forward a task assigned to them, to another user or work queue. Team leads can forward tasks that are not assigned to them. These tasks can be viewed in the Open Tasks page of the processing user's workspace or in the work queue workspace. Reallocate: This task action allows a user to remove the task from their inbox and re-run the allocation strategy that initially allocated the task at creation. Defer: This task action allows a user to set the task to Deferred status until the restart date. A task is deferred, and the task status is updated to Deferred . It will remain in the user's inbox and move into the My Deferred Tasks page. Restart: This task action allows a user to manually restart a deferred task and return it to the user's My Open Tasks list. Complete: This task action allows a user to update the status of a task to Completed . A task is completed and requires no further action.
